title: Increased cyclicity of atomic transitions via coherent interference of decay paths
authors: Eliza Cornell, Benjamin Pingault, Gergő Thiering, Neil Sinclair, Ádám Gali, Marko Lončar
abstract: Optical readout is a fundamental tool in atomic state measurement, yet the fidelity of optical readout is frequently limited by imperfect photon collection. This can be mitigated when readout occurs on a cycling transition which continuously fluoresces under resonant excitation, thus increasing signal and enabling single-shot readout. We present a method to extend the cyclicity of atomic transitions via coherent destructive interference between spurious decay paths. We describe the characteristics of atomic systems in which this method can be implemented and model several examples in which the number of emitted photons is increased by multiple orders of magnitude.
summary: This paper presents a method to dramatically improve the efficiency of optical state readout in quantum emitters by manipulating the decay pathways through coherent interference. By applying tailored external driving fields, the authors engineer artificial cycling transitions, enabling the emission of many more photons than previously possible. This technique offers a pathway to high-fidelity quantum measurements in solid-state systems like the NiV- center.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enhance the fidelity of optical readout in atomic state measurement, which is typically limited by imperfect photon collection efficiency.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that cyclicity can be significantly extended by engineering coherent destructive interference between spurious decay paths, leading to a massive increase in emitted photons.
method: The method involves applying strong coherent driving fields or auxiliary fields to induce artificial cycling transitions, circumventing limitations inherent in the native atomic decay pathways.
model_or_system: The study models atomic systems, using the negatively-charged nickel vacancy center (NiV-) in diamond as a prime example. The physics is described using a full master equation formalism involving ground and excited states.
key_observables: The number of emitted photons ($n_{	ext{ph},g_1}$) is the key diagnostic, alongside the branching ratio ($b$) which measures readout efficiency.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the strength of the driving fields ($\Omega_S$), detuning parameters ($\Delta_{aux}$), and the polarization dependence of the transition dipole moments (TDMs).
main_assumptions: The analysis often simplifies the system to two decaying excited states, and the strong drive approach requires careful polarization control and high optical powers.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between traditional readout (limited by pumping) and the enhanced readout using strong driving or auxiliary fields, showing orders of magnitude increases in photon counts.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the limitation of traditional readout, then introducing the strong drive approach to suppress unwanted decay paths, and finally detailing an auxiliary drive scheme to achieve even higher cyclicity with lower power.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides a powerful, controllable mechanism (coherent interference) to engineer fundamental quantum processes like spontaneous emission, which is crucial for quantum memory and readout.
